newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Domos silent on touchy Cuba plans.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Domos silent on touchy Cuba plans.

text.p: Mexico's Grupo Domos, which has earned the wrath of Washington for its partnership in Cuba's telephone company, declined comment on Thursday on news reports that it may pull out of the deal.
"We're not going to make any comment on the matter for now, we will make an official announcement when it's time," Domos spokeswoman Norma Lavin said. She declined to be more specific.
Domos, based in northern Mexico, bought 49 percent of Empresas de Telecomunicaciones de Cuba (ETECSA) in mid-1994, in a deal valued around $1.14 billion.
It later sold 29.29 percent of its stake to the Italian phone company Stet, but press reports have speculated it continued to have problems paying its share.

Its difficulties have been compounded by the so-called Helms-Burton Law, under which the United States threatened to sanction foreign firms it believed were "trafficking" in properties confiscated by Cuba's Communist government.

Last August, Domos' top executives received letters from the State Department warning them that their visas to the United States and those of their families could be withdrawn if the firm did not pull out of Cuba.

On Thursday, Reforma newspaper quoted unnamed analysts as saying Domos was months behind on its payments for the phone company, and was unable to obtain credit to honour the debt, which could force it to leave Cuba.
